name: “Why do you work so hard? Who are you trying to impress?”

lines.ref:
“Why do you work so hard?
Who are you trying to impress?”

shots.brief: crying or looking stressed/overwhelmed while working, selfie/tripod (ref: Woman in a bathrobe crying and dabbing her tears with a tissue at her desk; tripod)
graduation celebration footage (ref: Woman in academic graduation gown throwing mortarboard cap into the air; filmed by friend)
holding keys to new home/apartment, celebratory (ref: Woman excitedly dangling new house keys inside an empty house; filmed by friend)
working on laptop at home (ref: Woman working on laptop and talking in an aesthetic living room setup; tripod)
parents dining together, candid (ref: Parents sitting at fine dining restaurant table forming a heart with their hands over a birthday dessert; POV)
mirror selfie with parents or family (ref: Outdoor mirror selfie of daughter posing happily with both parents; mirror)
mirror selfie with parents or family (ref: Outdoor mirror selfie of daughter posing happily with both parents; mirror)
candid clip walking and laughing with parents on vacation (ref: Daughter walking arm-in-arm and laughing with parents in an alleyway; filmed by friend)
parents inspecting a home or renovation project (ref: Parents standing inside an active home renovation looking up at attic ladder; tripod)

special: Clips of parents or family members
Personal milestone clips (graduation, buying a house, crying/overwhelmed)
audit.notes: The format specifically relies on heartfelt personal clips of parents/family to deliver the emotional payoff after the question hook. Generic solo lifestyle footage cannot substitute for clips of the creator's parents.
audit.summary: A montage contrasting hard work and personal milestones (crying, graduation, buying a home, working late) with candid clips of the creator's parents to answer 'Who are you trying to impress?'.
